summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.1% YoY to INR77.8 crores, with EBITDA margin at 21.1% and record INR240+ crore order book.
summary.overview: Management called Q2 FY27 the strongest quarter in company history, with record revenue, EBITDA, PAT and EPS. Consolidated revenue grew 16.1% YoY and PAT grew 20.9%, with H1 PAT up 27.6% on 13.2% revenue growth. The total executed project order book reached a record above INR240 crores, including over INR100 crores (later stated as INR140 crores) in the newly set up aluminium window and facade division. Management says the INR100 crore capex programme (FY26 to FY28) is funded by internal accruals and debt, and extrusion capacity has been raised from 24,000 to 27,600 TPA.

segments.name: Polymer Products (PVC/uPVC profiles, windows, doors, panels)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR69.5 crores, up about 27% YoY; now about 89% of gross turnover vs 81% a year ago. Split of plastic products (about INR70 crores): PVC profile about INR54 crores and windows about INR16 crores.

segments.name: Modular Furniture (Dynasty)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR8.4 crores. H1 FY27 revenue about INR16 crores vs about INR23 crores in H1 FY26 due to project execution delays; management expects to catch up in H2. FY27 growth guided at 15-18%.

segments.name: Fluted panels
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue about INR29 crores; FY27 target about INR65 crores.

segments.name: Aluminium windows and facade (new division)
segments.commentary: Orders above INR100 crores (later stated as about INR140 crores in the order book); execution from Q3 FY27, revenue visible in Q4 FY27 (management expects about INR20 crores in FY27). Typical order size INR10 crores plus, execution 12-24 months.

guidance_outlook: Long-run revenue growth target of 25-30% YoY; no specific FY27 or FY28 guidance given.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected slightly better than FY26 (about 21%); new aluminium segment margins may run 2-3 points below the company average initially.
Around 60-70% of the order book expected to convert to revenue next year (FY28), with aluminium 18-24 month execution.
WPC door and wall-ceiling revenue for FY27 cut to about INR5-6 crores from an earlier INR15 crore expectation due to implementation delays.
Exports: FY27 target INR6-7 crores vs INR4.5 crores in FY26; INR3 crores plus already done in H1 FY27.
Modular furniture FY27 revenue expected to exceed FY26 level, per management.
capex_capacity: Extrusion capacity raised from 24,000 to 27,600 TPA; utilisation above 65% in H1 FY27 (vs 66% cited for FY26 in the question).
Plan to add about 8,000 MT extrusion capacity within 3-6 months; machine orders already placed.
INR100 crore capex programme over FY26-FY28 covering extrusion, WPC door and panel lines, and aluminium window and facade infrastructure at Jaipur; funded by internal accruals and debt.
Jaipur aluminium facility: one or two lines commissioned and trial done; full implementation expected by end FY27.
Existing capacity across plants could generate INR400 crores plus revenue, per management.
PP&E rose to INR117.2 crores (Sep 2026) from INR88.4 crores (Mar 2026), plus INR8.9 crores CWIP. Six plants across Jaipur, Bangalore and Coimbatore.
demand_pricing: Competition from Chinese imports in extrusion has largely faded over the last 2-3 years, per management; import tariffs have more than doubled to 3x, improving domestic competitiveness.
Export is for one European client in modular furniture (about 15% of modular revenue); other modular business is domestic.
Studio Arezzo retail (design-to-execution model, three studios) contributes about 20-22% of modular furniture revenue.
Around 65%+ of revenue from PVC extrusion B2B via 800+ channel partners.
Retention of 5% from running bills on uPVC/window/door/modular projects; retention receivables about INR8-10 crores; regular debtor cycle 30-45 days.
Management attributes margin gains to richer product mix (fluted and soffit panels, furniture profiles, higher-range doors and windows), not price hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Split of plastic products revenue and PVC vs uPVC windows.
qa_highlights.answer: Of about INR70 crores plastic products in Q2, about INR54 crores was PVC profile and about INR16 crores from windows division.

qa_highlights.question: Aluminium facade timeline: was it always Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no delay; executions start Q3 FY27 and revenue reflects in Q4 FY27. Orders closed; design approvals and structural calculations underway.

qa_highlights.question: Aluminium order book clients and order size.
qa_highlights.answer: Clients include Godrej, MR and M3M. Single orders typically INR10 crores plus; execution 12-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Order book split.
qa_highlights.answer: uPVC windows about INR70 crores, aluminium windows and facade about INR140 crores, modular furniture about INR30 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA margin driven by temporary price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said margins improved over 8-10 quarters due to refined product mix, not price hikes. FY25 fluted business was about INR38 crores vs INR30 crores in H1 FY27 (question wording was unclear on FY24 vs FY25).

qa_highlights.question: Receivables aging.
qa_highlights.answer: Over six months is essentially retention money (about INR8-10 crores); regular debtor cycle is 30-45 days. Full aging is derived only at year end.

risks_watch: Execution timing of the INR140 crore aluminium order book; revenue depends on civil site readiness, and new-segment margins may run 2-3 points lower.
WPC door launch delayed; FY27 revenue cut to INR5-6 crores from INR15 crores plan; FY28 contribution not quantified.
Modular furniture H1 revenue down to about INR16 crores from about INR23 crores; backlog catch-up needed in H2.
Retention receivables of about INR8-10 crores aged over six months; debt-funded capex raises leverage (D/E 0.68x).
Product-wise EBITDA margins not tracked; management to update later, so segment margin visibility is limited.
Several answers were vague or inconsistent (for example, capacity utilisation and volume figures), so they need checking against the presentation.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on order book, margins and the new aluminium vertical, but cautious and vague on specifics: no formal FY27 guidance, deferred WPC door and modular furniture targets, and several answers left for later calls.
key_quotes: We took our total executed project order book has reached an all-time high of more than INR240 crores, the highest in our company's 34-year history.
Our overall projection is to achieve 25% to 30% revenue growth in the longer run on a year-on-year basis.

adds.what: Extrusion capacity raised from 24,000 to 27,600 TPA (already done)
Plan to add about 8,000 MT extrusion capacity; machine orders placed
Jaipur aluminium window and facade facility: one or two lines commissioned, full implementation by end FY27

growth.why: Management gives a long-run 25-30% growth target with no FY27 total guide, but FY27 segment targets (fluted panels over INR65 crore, aluminium about INR20 crore, modular 15-18%) are backed by an order book above INR240 crore and an 8,000 MT extrusion addition with machines already ordered, though WPC doors were cut to INR5-6 crore.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 21.1% (+70 bps YoY) and H1 margin 22.0% (+180 bps), with management guiding FY27 margin slightly above FY26's ~21%, though new aluminium segment margins may run 2-3 points lower initially.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Extrusion capacity already raised from 24,000 to 27,600 TPA, and about 8,000 MT more is planned within 3-6 months with machine orders placed; Jaipur aluminium lines are commissioned with full implementation by end FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book above INR240 crore including about INR140 crore aluminium orders executing from Q3 FY27, and fluted panel FY27 target over INR65 crore against H1 of about INR29 crore; extrusion utilisation above 65% in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 65%, so no capex announcement is strictly needed for extrusion, but the INR100 crore FY26-FY28 programme is already in progress and the 8,000 MT addition is approved, making further announcements plausible rather than certain.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal FY27 total guidance is given; the long-run 25-30% growth target is held, while WPC door FY27 was cut to INR5-6 crore from INR15 crore and modular furniture H1 fell to about INR16 crore from INR23 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: WPC door FY27 cut to INR5-6 crore from INR15 crore, modular furniture H1 down about 30% YoY needs an H2 catch-up, and aluminium revenue depends on civil site readiness with about INR20 crore expected in FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aluminium windows and facade division starts execution in Q3 FY27 with revenue in Q4 FY27 (about INR20 crore in FY27), and WPC door launch is delayed but still planned at INR5-6 crore for FY27.

rows.label: Export growth to INR6-7 crore in FY27
rows.why: Exports at INR3 crore-plus already done in H1 FY27 against an FY27 target of INR6-7 crore versus INR4.5 crore in FY26.

rows.label: Aluminium order book conversion in FY28
rows.why: Management expects 60-70% of the above INR240 crore order book to convert to revenue in FY28, with aluminium execution of 18-24 months on orders of INR10 crore plus.

rows.label: Retention receivables aged over six months
rows.why: Retention receivables of about INR8-10 crore are aged over six months against a regular 30-45 day debtor cycle, and debt-funded capex has lifted D/E to 0.68x.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record order book, margin gains from mix and the new aluminium vertical, but cautious and vague on specifics such as FY27 total guidance, the WPC door cut and modular furniture catch-up; analysts pressed on the aluminium timeline, margin drivers and receivables aging.
